_about: Listening spaces for the binaural room renderer (stage.spatial.room, decision 0013). Dimensions in metres (length along the listener's look direction, width, height), the listener's position from the rear-left floor corner, and a target RT60 per octave band (125 Hz to 8 kHz). Wall absorption is derived from the target with Eyring's formula, so the early reflections and the late field describe the same room; 'absorption_bias' shifts it between walls, floor and ceiling (1 = average). Names are generic on purpose.

studio.label: Studio
studio.why: A treated control room, modelled on the measured SADIE II studio BRIRs (University of York, KU100 at the listening position): RT60 about 0.1 s in the mids and 0.2 s in the bass, direct-to-reverberant ratio about 11 dB for a frontal loudspeaker. That is drier than ITU-R BS.1116-3's 0.25 (V/100 m3)^(1/3) s upper guide, as rooms built for critical listening usually are. The reflected level is fitted to the measured front DRR (decision 0013).

living_room.label: Living room
living_room.why: A furnished domestic room. Measured furnished living rooms sit around 0.4 to 0.6 s at mid frequencies, longer in the bass where furniture absorbs little (Diaz and Pedrero 2005, Applied Acoustics 66).

car.label: Car
car.why: A car cabin is tiny and full of soft seats and glass: reverberation times of about 0.05 to 0.1 s, with strong very early reflections from the windscreen and side glass. The listener sits on the centre line: in the driver's seat the right-hand virtual loudspeaker would be 15 cm from the door, and that near-equal reflection combs the treble by more than the timbre matcher may correct (decision 0013).

club.label: Club
club.why: A mid-sized club room treated for amplified music: around 0.8 to 1 s mid-band, with a longer low end that the bass crossover keeps out of the render.

concert_hall.label: Concert hall
concert_hall.why: A large shoebox hall. Beranek (Concert Halls and Opera Houses, 2004) reports about 1.8 to 2.1 s occupied mid-frequency reverberation in the best-rated halls, with a bass ratio above 1.1 and a high-frequency roll-off from air absorption.

cinema.label: Cinema
cinema.why: A mid-sized auditorium. Cinema guidelines aim for a short, even decay so dialogue stays clear in a large volume: about 0.5 to 0.7 s mid-band for 2000 to 3000 m3, rising slightly in the bass.

dry_stage.label: Dry stage
dry_stage.why: A minimally reflective room for object rendering (decision 0025): a small, well-treated space whose only job is to give each direct sound a few short, low-level early reflections so that it is heard outside the head, as the research on non-individual HRTFs asks (Reed and Maher; Rajendran et al.). RT60 about 0.05 to 0.14 s, reflections 6 dB under the studio's fitted level, image sources to order 2 in a 7 m room so every reflection arrives within 80 ms of the direct sound. The long tail is not here on purpose: the record's own reverb, returned by dereverberation, supplies the ambience.
